children: Jefferies kept Buy and $575 target on Microsoft (MSFT) after Copilot upgrades — Cowork, Code, Autopilot — which could boost enterprise AI spending and subscription and usage monetization.
Microsoft expanded Copilot into a unified hub—Home, Code and Autopilot—and will launch Autopilot in private preview by end of September, aiming to keep users and AI tools inside its ecosystem.
Microsoft (MSFT) kept about a 27% stake in OpenAI after October 2025 restructuring. Agreement preserves Microsoft’s joint intellectual-property rights tied to their collaboration through 2032.
Microsoft (MSFT) is integrating OpenAI’s Dots AI agents into Microsoft 365, letting Dots run under Microsoft 365’s enterprise security and governance controls for corporate deployments.
Microsoft (MSFT) shares slipped ~1.2% to $503.32 at 10:10 a.m. ET after an announcement. Traders questioned if higher paid use of Microsoft 365 and Azure will cover added compute and support costs.
Microsoft (MSFT) shares are up ~6% year-to-date. Traders note ongoing debate over ROI from AI investments and muted market sentiment versus broader AI hype, affecting short-term outlook.
MSFT: TomTom location services added to Microsoft Marketplace and eligible under Azure MACC, letting Microsoft customers procure TomTom location intelligence through existing Azure MACC agreements.
